title: Incorrect parameters information exposed through ClassDB bindings
body: **Godot Version** 2c089e9bf0b8712d0bc444c2ceaf9c543ed9c777 **Issue Description** Recently, while looking through potential issues in godot, I discovered that for `MeshConvexDecompositionSettings`, the `set_resolution` function connected via `D_METHOD`, is using the argument name `min_volume_per_convex_hull` instead of `resolution`. As a result code hints in editor are incorrect (the docs looks unaffected). https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/2c089e9bf0b8712d0bc444c2ceaf9c543ed9c777/scene/resources/mesh.cpp#L158-L162 https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/2c089e9bf0b8712d0bc444c2ceaf9c543ed9c777/scene/resources/mesh.h#L268-L271 So it looks that there is currently no CI validation for this kind of issues, so mistakes like this can easily be made. A more comprehensive solution would probably be to add a CI validation script that catches these issues during the build, not in runtime. While experimenting, I found a few categories of issues that could be detected automatically: - Validate parameter names between the C++ declaration and `D_METHOD` There may be cases where intentionally using different names is desirable (for example, if we want more user friendly names in the Gdscript than in the C++ implementation), so enforcing identical names everywhere might not be always appropriate. However, I think having a validation step would completely eliminate accidental mismatches like the one above. ``` core/config/project_settings.cpp:1621: 'has_setting' (ProjectSettings::has_setting) param[0]: D_METHOD='name' C++='var' core/config/project_settings.cpp:1622: 'set_setting' (ProjectSettings::set_setting) param[0]: D_METHOD='name' C++='setting' core/config/project_settings.cpp:1623: 'get_setting' (ProjectSettings::get_setting) param[0]: D_METHOD='name' C++='setting' core/config/project_settings.cpp:1627: 'set_order' (ProjectSettings::set_order) param[1]: D_METHOD='position' C++='order' scene/resources/material.cpp:3546: 'set_stencil_compare' (BaseMaterial3D::set_stencil_compare) param[0]: D_METHOD='stencil_compare' C++='op' scene/resources/mesh.cpp:161: 'set_resolution' (MeshConvexDecompositionSettings::set_resolution) param[0]: D_METHOD='min_volume_per_convex_hull' C++='resolution' ``` - Validate that signals are emitted with the correct number of arguments ``` editor/scene/scene_tree_editor.cpp:119: emit_signal('open'): 1 arg emitted but signal declared with 0 params editor/scene/scene_tree_editor.cpp:124: emit_signal('open_script'): 1 arg emitted but signal declared with 0 params editor/scene/scene_tree_editor.cpp:1644: emit_signal('node_prerename'): 2 args emitted but signal declared with 0 params scene/gui/graph_frame.cpp:244: emit_signal('autoshrink_changed'): 1 arg emitted but signal declared with 0 params editor/audio/editor_audio_buses.cpp:756: emit_signal('dropped'): 2 args emitted but signal declared with 0 params ``` https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/2c089e9bf0b8712d0bc444c2ceaf9c543ed9c777/scene/gui/graph_frame.cpp#L202 https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/2c089e9bf0b8712d0bc444c2ceaf9c543ed9c777/scene/gui/graph_frame.cpp#L244 - Validate that `ADD_PROPERTY` uses the correct property type ``` modules/openxr/extensions/spatial_entities/openxr_spatial_marker_tracking.cpp:395: property 'bounds_size': Variant::INT but setter 'set_bounds_size' takes 'Vector2' modules/openxr/extensions/spatial_entities/openxr_spatial_plane_tracking.cpp:273: property 'bounds_size': Variant::INT but setter 'set_bounds_size' takes 'Vector2' servers/audio/effects/audio_effect_pitch_shift.cpp:363: property 'oversampling': Variant::FLOAT but setter 'set_oversampling' takes 'int' ``` https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/2c089e9bf0b8712d0bc444c2ceaf9c543ed9c777/modules/openxr/extensions/spatial_entities/openxr_spatial_marker_tracking.cpp#L395 https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/2c089e9bf0b8712d0bc444c2ceaf9c543ed9c777/modules/openxr/extensions/spatial_entities/openxr_spatial_marker_tracking.h#L219 - Validate getter/setter naming consistency this one just feels a bit odd to me. When a property is called `abc` convention is to use `set_abc`/`is_abc`/`get_abc` functions, but some getters/setters changes here the names into something like `is_abc_enabled` or `set_abc_mode`, which makes things a bit inconsistent. ``` scene/2d/light_2d.cpp:483: property 'offset': setter 'set_texture_offset' doesn't follow 'set_offset' convention modules/visual_shader/visual_shader.cpp:4748: property 'autoshrink': setter 'set_autoshrink_enabled' doesn't follow 'set_autoshrink' convention scene/3d/light_3d.cpp:655: property 'omni_shadow_mode': getter 'get_shadow_mode' doesn't follow 'get/is_omni_shadow_mode' convention scene/gui/control.cpp:4958: property 'grow_vertical': setter 'set_v_grow_direction' doesn't follow 'set_grow_vertical' convention scene/main/canvas_item.cpp:1593: property 'z_as_relative': getter 'is_z_relative' doesn't follow 'get/is_z_as_relative' convention ```
